paragraphs.title: Bildad's Rebuke and the Fixed Order

easy.explanation: The passage begins, “Then answered Bildad the Shuhite.”
easy.q: Who spoke at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: Bildad asks, “How long will it be ere ye make an end of words?”
easy.q: What does Bildad want them to stop doing?

easy.explanation: Bildad asks, “Shall the earth be forsaken for thee?”
easy.q: For whose sake, according to Bildad, should the earth not be forsaken?

medium.explanation: He says, “mark, and afterwards we will speak.”
medium.q: What does Bildad suggest doing before speaking further?

medium.explanation: Bildad is telling Job to stop continuing with so many words.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “make an end of words” mean in context?

answers: The world should change for Job
The earth's order will not change for one person
medium.explanation: He asks whether the earth should be forsaken or the rock removed for Job's sake.
medium.q: What general claim does Bildad make in these verses?

answers: He rejects the idea that they should be counted as beasts
He agrees that they are beasts
challenge.explanation: Bildad asks, “Wherefore are we counted as beasts, and reputed vile in your sight?”
challenge.q: How does Bildad respond to Job's apparent contempt for his companions?

answers: A person's anger cannot change the order of the world
The earth is angry with the person
The rock is the wicked person's dwelling
challenge.explanation: Bildad presents Job's anger as unable to alter the established order of creation.
challenge.q: What is the connection between “He teareth himself in his anger” and the questions about the earth and rock?

answers: Consider the matter first and then speak
challenge.explanation: His instruction is to “mark, and afterwards we will speak.”
challenge.q: What practical instruction comes from Bildad's words?

paragraphs.title: The Wicked Person's Light Is Extinguished and He Is Trapped

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the light of the wicked shall be put out.”
easy.q: What happens to the light of the wicked?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “The steps of his strength shall be straitened.”
easy.q: What happens to the steps of the wicked person's strength?

easy.explanation: The passage mentions a net, a snare, a gin, and a trap.

answers: His own counsel casts him down
medium.explanation: The verse says, “his own counsel shall cast him down.”
medium.q: What is the connection between the wicked person's counsel and his fall?

medium.explanation: A snare is a trap, fitting the passage's images of nets and hidden dangers.
medium.q: What does “snare” mean in this passage?

answers: From extinguished light to narrowed steps and traps
From a safe home to greater light
medium.explanation: The light goes out, the steps become narrow, and the person is caught by snares.
medium.q: How does the description develop in verses 5–10?

answers: The danger is concealed along the way
challenge.explanation: The trap is “laid for him in the ground,” showing that the danger is hidden.
challenge.q: What does the hidden snare in the ground teach about the danger on the wicked person's path?

answers: A weakening and restricting of his condition
challenge.explanation: His light diminishes and his steps are restricted, showing his worsening condition.
challenge.q: What idea is repeated both in the extinguished light and the narrowed steps?

challenge.explanation: The text directly says that “his own counsel shall cast him down.”
challenge.q: What causes the wicked person's downfall according to verse 7?

paragraphs.title: Terrors, Disaster, and the Ruin of the Home

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Terrors shall make him afraid on every side.”
His strength is described as being “hungerbitten.”
The verses describe his tabernacle and habitation.
easy.q: What is described as being damaged or destroyed?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “destruction shall be ready at his side.”
medium.q: What is ready beside the wicked person?

medium.explanation: The expression describes death as a powerful force devouring his strength.
medium.q: What does “the firstborn of death” signify in this context?

answers: Terrors, weakening, and destruction of body and home
A secure home, great strength, and joy
medium.explanation: Terrors surround him, his strength fails, and his body and dwelling are consumed.
medium.q: What order of decline is described in the passage?

answers: It is limited to the road
It affects the person and his home
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the devouring of his strength and the destruction of his tabernacle.
challenge.q: What does the mention of his skin, strength, and tabernacle show about the extent of the disaster?

answers: He is brought under the power of terror
challenge.explanation: His confidence is removed and he is brought to the king of terrors, showing terror's domination over him.
challenge.q: What does being brought to “the king of terrors” mean in the passage?

answers: It emphasizes the destruction of his home
It shows that his tent is safe
challenge.explanation: Brimstone scattered upon the habitation intensifies the image of ruin.
challenge.q: What does the scattering of brimstone upon his habitation add to the description?

paragraphs.title: Loss of Roots, Name, and Remnant

easy.explanation: The verse says, “His roots shall be dried up beneath.”
easy.q: What happens to the roots of the wicked person?

answers: It is preserved in his house
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “His remembrance shall perish from the earth.”

answers: He has neither son nor nephew, and no remnant remains
easy.explanation: The passage says he shall have “neither son nor nephew” and no remaining people in his dwellings.
easy.q: What is said about his descendants and any remaining people in his dwelling?

answers: Both roots and branches are affected
The wicked person rises from the earth
medium.explanation: His roots dry up beneath, while his branch is cut off above.
medium.q: What is shown by the contrast between “beneath” and “above”?

answers: From light into darkness and out of the world
From the wilderness into his home
medium.explanation: The verse says he is driven “from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.”
medium.q: Where is the wicked person driven?

medium.explanation: Those after him are “astonied,” and those before him are “affrighted.”
medium.q: How do those who come after and those who went before respond to his fate?

answers: No personal or family remembrance remains
challenge.explanation: His remembrance perishes, he has no name in the street, and no descendant or remnant remains.
challenge.q: What is the significance of losing both his name and his descendants?

challenge.explanation: Their astonishment and fear emphasize the severity of his downfall.
challenge.q: What do the reactions of later and earlier generations indicate about his fate?

answers: To one who does not know God
challenge.explanation: The final verse speaks of “him that knoweth not God.”
challenge.q: To whom is such a fate attributed at the end of the passage?
